chunks: ʿUmar ibn Yazīd asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the narration which they relate: that it is not appropriate to perform supererogatory prayer at the time of every obligatory prayer.
He asked, “What is the limit of this time?” So he said, “When the one giving the iqāmah begins the iqāmah.”
He said to him, “The people differ regarding the iqāmah.” He said, “The one giving the iqāmah is the one with whom the prayer is performed.”

key_terms.الرِّوَايَةِ: the transmitted report being asked about
key_terms.الْإِقَامَةِ: the call immediately preceding the start of salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْمُقِيمُ: the one who gives the iqāmah for the prayer
key_terms.وَقْتِ: the relevant time or period under discussion
key_terms.يُتَطَوَّعَ: to perform a voluntary or supererogatory prayer

ai.seo_question: When does the time begin in which one should stop supererogatory prayer before the obligatory congregational prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling about when supererogatory prayer should cease before an obligatory congregational prayer. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام defines the relevant time as the beginning of the iqāmah of the imam or prayer leader with whom the congregational prayer is actually being established.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1135 - Umar ibn Yazid asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) about the narration that states it is not appropriate to perform supererogatory (nafl) prayers at the time of every obligatory (fardh) prayer.
He asked: "What is the limit for this time?"
He (as) replied: "When the person giving the iqamah (call immediately preceding the prayer) begins the iqamah."
Umar said: "People differ in the timing of the iqamah."
He (as) responded: "The one giving the iqamah is the one with whom the prayer is being established”.
